name: What is the difference between painting and staining cabin interior wood?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between painting and staining cabin interior wood?

acceptedAnswer.text: Paint covers the wood grain with a solid film, while stain penetrates and highlights the natural grain, knots, and texture of logs and pine paneling. Painting a cabin interior creates a bright, modern finish, but future chipping or peeling can be difficult to reverse on rough wood. Staining preserves the rustic character and allows the wood to breathe, though it requires consistent wood tone underneath. The practical tradeoff is aesthetic: paint conceals water stains and mismatched repairs, whereas stain celebrates original woodwork and requires meticulous surface preparation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Stain penetrates the wood to highlight natural grain and texture, while paint coats the surface with solid color, hiding imperfections but masking the wood's original character.
